result.summary: This unit is sentry-native's vendor directory: the acutest unit-test header, the jsmn JSON tokenizer, the MPack 1.0 MessagePack amalgamation (allocator routed to sentry_malloc/sentry_free), and the stb_sprintf formatter. I read every file and found no network use, no encoded payloads, no load-time constructors, no hooking, no reading of secrets, and no hidden behaviour. The code matches the upstream libraries apart from the expected sentry allocator integration.

findings.title: Test harness checks for an attached debugger
findings.detail: Acutest's test runner reads /proc/self/status for TracerPid, and on Windows calls IsDebuggerPresent(). It uses the result only to stop forking each test into a child process when a debugger is attached. This is documented upstream acutest behaviour that makes debugging easier. It hides nothing, and it exists only in the test-harness main(), not in library code.

findings.title: MPack allocator redirected to sentry allocator
findings.detail: The vendored MPack 1.0 amalgamation sets MPACK_MALLOC to sentry_malloc and MPACK_FREE to sentry_free, declared extern in mpack.c. This is sentry-native's usual integration change: it routes allocations through sentry's allocator. It is not a hook or a function replacement.

findings.title: stb_sprintf supports %n
findings.detail: stb_sprintf supports the %n specifier, which writes through a pointer argument. This is standard upstream behaviour and a hazard only if a caller passes an untrusted format string. It is not a deliberate weakness.

data_flows.what: MessagePack-encoded data supplied by the calling code
data_flows.to: A local file whose path the caller passes to mpack_writer_init_filename / mpack_writer_init_stdfile (sentry uses this for its own envelope and run state)

data_flows.what: Unit-test results (test names, durations, pass or fail) and the test command line. Only in the test-runner main(), which is compiled only for sentry's own tests.
data_flows.to: A file named by the --xml-output option, and child test processes started with fork or CreateProcessA
